source.primary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments, 4th c. CE ~330-360). NB: Codex Vaticanus (B/03) does NOT contain Revelation in its original 4th-c. hand.
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Alexandrinus (A/02; British Library Royal 1 D. V-VIII, 5th c. CE) — for Revelation often preferred to Sinaiticus on internal grounds. Codex Ephraemi Rescriptus (C/04; 5th c., palimpsest).
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: P47 (Chester Beatty III; 3rd c. CE ~250) DOES NOT preserve Rev 6 — P47 begins at Rev 9:10. P115 (P.Oxy 4499; 3rd-4th c.) preserves portions of Rev 2-15 lacunosely; some fragments touch Rev 6. P18 (P.Oxy 1079; 3rd-4th c.) preserves Rev 1:4-7. For Rev 6, the earliest substantial witnesses are 4th-c. Sinaiticus + 5th-c. Alexandrinus + Ephraemi.
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017). Hoskier 1929.
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Sinaiticus + Alexandrinus + Ephraemi original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus + Hoskier 1929
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference + Hoskier 1929.
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Hoskier 1929. Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + (4th c.). Codex Alexandrinus: British Library Royal 1 D. V-VIII (5th c.). Aune WBC 1997-1998 (vol 2 covers ch. 6); Beale NIGTC 1999; Charles ICC 1920; Koester AB 2014; Mounce NICNT 1997 rev.; Bauckham *The Climax of Prophecy* (T&T Clark 1993); Caird *Revelation* (BNTC 1966); Levine-Brettler JANT 2017. For the Zechariah-1/Zechariah-6 horsemen background: Petersen *Haggai and Zechariah 1-8* (OTL 1984).
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form as transmitted via SBLGNT. Rev 6 contains the Four Horsemen pericope (vv.1-8) — one of the most reception-historically-loaded passages in Western literature and art. The cosmic-signs catalogue (vv.12-17) is the densest single-pericope cross-corpus to the Olivet Discourse + Joel + Isa 13 + Isa 34 + Ezek 32 + Mark 13 + Luke 21 + Acts 2. The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua. Nomina sacra appear abbreviated.

verses.text: Καὶ εἶδον ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὸ ἀρνίον μίαν ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ σφραγίδων, καὶ ἤκουσα ἑνὸς ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων λέγοντος ὡς φωνὴ βροντῆς· Ἔρχου.
verses.translit: Kai eidon hote ēnoixen to arnion mian ek tōn hepta sphragidōn, kai ēkousa henos ek tōn tessarōn zōōn legontos hōs phōnē brontēs· Erchou.
verses.notes: **FIRST SEAL OPENING**. *to arnion* (the Lamb — the slain-yet-standing Lamb of Rev 5). *henos ek tōn tessarōn zōōn* — one of the four living creatures (chayyot, cf. ch. 4) speaks. *Erchou* (Come) — addressed to the rider, not the visionary. Variant: some Western witnesses + later Byzantine read *Erchou kai ide* ("come and see") — likely a scribal expansion harmonizing the four invocations. NA28/SBLGNT prefer the shorter *Erchou*.

verses.text: καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος λευκός, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἔχων τόξον, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ στέφανος, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν νικῶν καὶ ἵνα νικήσῃ.
verses.translit: kai eidon, kai idou hippos leukos, kai ho kathēmenos ep’ auton echōn toxon, kai edothē autō stephanos, kai exēlthen nikōn kai hina nikēsē.
verses.notes: **FIRST HORSEMAN — WHITE HORSE**. *hippos leukos* + bow + crown + conquering. **MAJOR INTERPRETIVE CRUX**: (a) **Conquest** (Aune, Caird, Mounce — preferred by majority of modern scholars: the white-horse is the Parthian-bowman archetype, evoking the menace of Rome's Eastern enemy; Parthians were known as the world's premier mounted-archers); (b) **Christ/Gospel** (Irenaeus *Adv. Haer.* 4.21.3; many medieval/Reformation readings: the white-horse rider is the victorious gospel-Christ, paralleling Rev 19:11-16 where Christ rides a white horse); (c) **Antichrist/false-Christ** (Beale: a parody of Christ — the imitative-deceptive figure). Cross-corpus **Zech 1:8 + 6:1-8** (the four colored horse-and-chariot patrols going to the four winds). **HIGH LENS-RISK FLAG**: the white-horseman is heavily engaged in heterodox readings; do not pre-resolve.

verses.text: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν δευτέραν, ἤκουσα τοῦ δευτέρου ζῴου λέγοντος· Ἔρχου.
verses.translit: Kai hote ēnoixen tēn sphragida tēn deuteran, ēkousa tou deuterou zōou legontos· Erchou.

verses.text: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἄλλος ἵππος πυρρός, καὶ τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἐδόθη αὐτῷ λαβεῖν τὴν εἰρήνην ἐκ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἵνα ἀλλήλους σφάξουσιν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ μάχαιρα μεγάλη.
verses.translit: kai exēlthen allos hippos pyrros, kai tō kathēmenō ep’ auton edothē autō labein tēn eirēnēn ek tēs gēs kai hina allēlous sphaxousin, kai edothē autō machaira megalē.
verses.notes: **SECOND HORSEMAN — RED HORSE / WAR**. *hippos pyrros* (fire-red horse). Civil-war imagery (*allēlous sphaxousin* — they slaughter one another). *machaira megalē* (great sword) — Roman *gladius*. Cross-corpus Zech 1:8 (the red horses among the myrtles).

verses.text: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν τρίτην, ἤκουσα τοῦ τρίτου ζῴου λέγοντος· Ἔρχου. καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος μέλας, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἔχων ζυγὸν ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Kai hote ēnoixen tēn sphragida tēn tritēn, ēkousa tou tritou zōou legontos· Erchou. kai eidon, kai idou hippos melas, kai ho kathēmenos ep’ auton echōn zygon en tē cheiri autou.
verses.notes: **THIRD HORSEMAN — BLACK HORSE / FAMINE**. *zygon* (balance / scales) — economic-rationing image. Cross-corpus Ezek 4:10, 16 (siege-rationing); Lam 5:10.

verses.text: καὶ ἤκουσα ὡς φωνὴν ἐν μέσῳ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων λέγουσαν· Χοῖνιξ σίτου δηναρίου, καὶ τρεῖς χοίνικες κριθῶν δηναρίου· καὶ τὸ ἔλαιον καὶ τὸν οἶνον μὴ ἀδικήσῃς.
verses.translit: kai ēkousa hōs phōnēn en mesō tōn tessarōn zōōn legousan· Choinix sitou dēnariou, kai treis choinikes krithōn dēnariou· kai to elaion kai ton oinon mē adikēsēs.
verses.notes: **FAMINE-PRICING ORACLE**. *choinix sitou dēnariou* = 1 quart of wheat for 1 denarius (= 1 day's wage — Matt 20:2). Roman price-records (e.g., Cicero *Verr.* 3.81; Polybius 2.15.1) suggest the normal price was 1 denarius per 8-16 choinikes — so this is famine-pricing at 8-16x normal. *to elaion kai ton oinon mē adikēsēs* (do not harm oil and wine) — the staple-grain crisis spares luxury-crops. Possibly historical reference to Domitian's 92 CE edict to halve provincial vineyards (Suetonius *Domitian* 7.2), provoking protests.

verses.text: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν τετάρτην, ἤκουσα φωνὴν τοῦ τετάρτου ζῴου λέγοντος· Ἔρχου.
verses.translit: Kai hote ēnoixen tēn sphragida tēn tetartēn, ēkousa phōnēn tou tetartou zōou legontos· Erchou.

verses.text: καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος χλωρός, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ ὄνομα αὐτῷ ὁ Θάνατος, καὶ ὁ ᾅδης ἠκολούθει μετ’ αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἐξουσία ἐπὶ τὸ τέταρτον τῆς γῆς, ἀποκτεῖναι ἐν ῥομφαίᾳ καὶ ἐν λιμῷ καὶ ἐν θανάτῳ καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν θηρίων τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: kai eidon, kai idou hippos chlōros, kai ho kathēmenos epanō autou onoma autō ho Thanatos, kai ho hadēs ēkolouthei met’ autou· kai edothē autois exousia epi to tetarton tēs gēs, apokteinai en rhomphaia kai en limō kai en thanatō kai hypo tōn thēriōn tēs gēs.
verses.notes: **FOURTH HORSEMAN — PALE-GREEN HORSE / DEATH**. *hippos chlōros* — *chlōros* properly = greenish-yellow / sickly green (the color of vegetation, of unripe-fruit, of corpses). The traditional English 'pale' translation flattens the morbid-green nuance. *ho Thanatos* (Death) named-rider + Hades following. *exousia epi to tetarton tēs gēs* (authority over a quarter of the earth). Four-fold death-mode: sword + famine + plague + wild-beasts. Cross-corpus **Ezek 14:21 LXX** (the four classic Ezekielian judgments: sword, famine, wild beasts, plague). The Horsemen-tetrad → Ezekiel-tetrad mapping.

verses.text: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν πέμπτην σφραγῖδα, εἶδον ὑποκάτω τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν ἐσφαγμένων διὰ τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ διὰ τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἣν εἶχον.
verses.translit: Kai hote ēnoixen tēn pemptēn sphragida, eidon hypokatō tou thysiastēriou tas psychas tōn esphagmenōn dia ton logon tou theou kai dia tēn martyrian hēn eichon.
verses.notes: **FIFTH SEAL — MARTYRS UNDER THE ALTAR**. *hypokatō tou thysiastēriou* (under the altar) — cross-corpus Lev 4:7, 18, 25, 30, 34 (the blood of sacrificial victims poured at the base of the altar); m. Yoma 5:6. The martyrs identified with sacrificial-blood. Major martyr-theology site.

verses.text: καὶ ἔκραξαν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγοντες· Ἕως πότε, ὁ δεσπότης ὁ ἅγιος καὶ ἀληθινός, οὐ κρίνεις καὶ ἐκδικεῖς τὸ αἷμα ἡμῶν ἐκ τῶν κατοικούντων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς;
verses.translit: kai ekraxan phōnē megalē legontes· Heōs pote, ho despotēs ho hagios kai alēthinos, ou krineis kai ekdikeis to haima hēmōn ek tōn katoikountōn epi tēs gēs?
verses.notes: **MARTYRS' COMPLAINT — *HEŌS POTE***. *Heōs pote* (How long?) — biblical lament-formula (cross-corpus Ps 6:3; 13:1-2; 35:17; 74:10; 89:46; 94:3; Hab 1:2; Zech 1:12). *ekdikeis* — vengeance-vocabulary (cross-corpus Deut 32:43 LXX *ekdikēsei haima huiōn autou*). The vengeance-petition has been theologically debated since patristics.

verses.text: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἑκάστῳ στολὴ λευκή, καὶ ἐρρέθη αὐτοῖς ἵνα ἀναπαύσωνται ἔτι χρόνον μικρόν, ἕως πληρωθῶσιν καὶ οἱ σύνδουλοι αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτῶν οἱ μέλλοντες ἀποκτέννεσθαι ὡς καὶ αὐτοί.
verses.translit: kai edothē autois hekastō stolē leukē, kai errethē autois hina anapausōntai eti chronon mikron, heōs plērōthōsin kai hoi syndouloi autōn kai hoi adelphoi autōn hoi mellontes apoktennesthai hōs kai autoi.
verses.notes: White robes + delay-for-full-number-of-martyrs. Cross-corpus 4 Ezra 4:35-37 (the rabbinic-apocalyptic 'predetermined number of the righteous').

verses.text: Καὶ εἶδον ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν ἕκτην, καὶ σεισμὸς μέγας ἐγένετο, καὶ ὁ ἥλιος ἐγένετο μέλας ὡς σάκκος τρίχινος, καὶ ἡ σελήνη ὅλη ἐγένετο ὡς αἷμα,
verses.translit: Kai eidon hote ēnoixen tēn sphragida tēn hektēn, kai seismos megas egeneto, kai ho hēlios egeneto melas hōs sakkos trichinos, kai hē selēnē holē egeneto hōs haima,
verses.notes: **MAJOR COSMIC-SIGNS VERSE — SIXTH SEAL**. *seismos megas* (great earthquake) + sun darkened to sackcloth-black + moon to blood. **DENSE CROSS-CORPUS**: **Joel 2:30-31** LXX / 3:3-4 LXX (sun to darkness + moon to blood); **Isa 13:10** (cosmic darkening at day of the Lord); **Isa 34:4** (the heavens rolled up); **Ezek 32:7-8** (sun darkened + moon withholding light); **Mark 13:24-25** + **Matt 24:29** + **Luke 21:25-26** (Olivet Discourse cosmic signs); **Acts 2:19-20** (Peter's Pentecost-Joel citation). *sakkos trichinos* (sackcloth of hair — coarse black goat-hair sackcloth used for mourning). **MAJOR LENS-RISK FLAG**: this is one of the most-engaged eschatological-signs verses in heterodox and Raëlian readings (Raël *The End of the World* engages this whole pericope vv.12-14 explicitly). Acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework applies. **EDITOR DO NOT PRE-RESOLVE** toward (a) conventional apocalyptic 'cosmic dissolution' reading, (b) preterist 70-CE fulfillment reading, (c) historical-eclipse reading, or (d) Raëlian end-time / cosmic-disturbance reading.

verses.text: καὶ οἱ ἀστέρες τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἔπεσαν εἰς τὴν γῆν, ὡς συκῆ βάλλει τοὺς ὀλύνθους αὐτῆς ὑπὸ ἀνέμου μεγάλου σειομένη,
verses.translit: kai hoi asteres tou ouranou epesan eis tēn gēn, hōs sykē ballei tous olynthous autēs hypo anemou megalou seiomenē,
verses.notes: **STARS FALLING TO EARTH**. *hoi asteres tou ouranou epesan eis tēn gēn* (the stars of heaven fell to the earth). Simile: as a fig-tree drops its unripe-figs (*olynthous*) in a wind-shaking. Cross-corpus **Isa 34:4** LXX (*pesetai panta ta astra hōs phylla apo ampelou*); **Mark 13:25** + Matt 24:29 (*hoi asteres esontai ek tou ouranou piptontes*). The fig-tree-shake simile parallels the Lukan fig-tree parable (Luke 21:29-31). **LENS-RISK FLAG**: heterodox readings (including Raëlian) sometimes engage this verse as meteor / asteroid / falling-craft imagery; preserve the apocalyptic-Isa 34 surface.

verses.text: καὶ ὁ οὐρανὸς ἀπεχωρίσθη ὡς βιβλίον ἑλισσόμενον, καὶ πᾶν ὄρος καὶ νῆσος ἐκ τῶν τόπων αὐτῶν ἐκινήθησαν.
verses.translit: kai ho ouranos apechōristhē hōs biblion helissomenon, kai pan oros kai nēsos ek tōn topōn autōn ekinēthēsan.
verses.notes: **HEAVENS ROLLED UP**. *ho ouranos apechōristhē hōs biblion helissomenon* (the heaven was split apart like a scroll being rolled up). Cross-corpus **Isa 34:4** LXX (*helichthēsetai ho ouranos hōs biblion*); Heb 1:12; 2 Pet 3:10. Tectonic-disturbance: every mountain and island moved. Cross-corpus Jer 4:24.

verses.text: καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς καὶ οἱ μεγιστᾶνες καὶ οἱ χιλίαρχοι καὶ οἱ πλούσιοι καὶ οἱ ἰσχυροὶ καὶ πᾶς δοῦλος καὶ ἐλεύθερος ἔκρυψαν ἑαυτοὺς εἰς τὰ σπήλαια καὶ εἰς τὰς πέτρας τῶν ὀρέων·
verses.translit: kai hoi basileis tēs gēs kai hoi megistanes kai hoi chiliarchoi kai hoi plousioi kai hoi ischyroi kai pas doulos kai eleutheros ekrypsan heautous eis ta spēlaia kai eis tas petras tōn oreōn·
verses.notes: **SEVEN-FOLD SOCIAL-HIERARCHY**. Kings + magnates + chiliarchs (military commanders) + rich + strong + every slave + free. Universal-rank catalogue. Hiding in caves + among rocks. Cross-corpus **Isa 2:10, 19, 21**.

verses.text: καὶ λέγουσιν τοῖς ὄρεσιν καὶ ταῖς πέτραις· Πέσετε ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς καὶ κρύψατε ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς ὀργῆς τοῦ ἀρνίου,
verses.translit: kai legousin tois oresin kai tais petrais· Pesete eph’ hēmas kai krypsate hēmas apo prosōpou tou kathēmenou epi tou thronou kai apo tēs orgēs tou arniou,
verses.notes: **THE MOUNTAINS-FALL-ON-US PRAYER**. *Pesete eph’ hēmas kai krypsate hēmas* (Fall on us and hide us). Direct cross-corpus **Hos 10:8** LXX (*erousi tois oresin Kalypsate hēmas, kai tois bounois Pesate eph’ hēmas*); cf. **Luke 23:30** (Jesus' word to the daughters of Jerusalem, citing Hosea). *apo tēs orgēs tou arniou* (from the wrath of the Lamb) — striking oxymoron: lamb + wrath.

verses.text: ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ἡμέρα ἡ μεγάλη τῆς ὀργῆς αὐτῶν, καὶ τίς δύναται σταθῆναι;
verses.translit: hoti ēlthen hē hēmera hē megalē tēs orgēs autōn, kai tis dynatai stathēnai?
verses.notes: **THE GREAT DAY OF WRATH**. *hē hēmera hē megalē tēs orgēs* — cross-corpus **Joel 2:11, 31** LXX; Zeph 1:14-18; Nahum 1:6; Mal 3:2. Variant: NA28/SBLGNT read *autōn* (their wrath — referring to both the one on the throne and the Lamb of v.16); Sinaiticus + Alexandrinus + Ephraemi support *autou* (his — referring only to the Lamb). The plural *autōn* is the harder reading and accepted in modern critical editions. *tis dynatai stathēnai* (who is able to stand?) — cross-corpus Nahum 1:6; Mal 3:2; Ps 76:7 (75:8 LXX); Joel 2:11. Chapter ends with the rhetorical question — sets up the 144,000 sealed of Rev 7.
